goal: Build independent conventional business applications driven by one shared intelligent runtime, while keeping the group cockpit as the command and observation layer.
current_stage: Enterprise Application Foundation and Intelligent Workflow Integration
next_stage: Deepen Growth & Sales, Manufacturing ERP and Smart Park with domain-specific records, state machines and object-write-back workflows.
product_principles: The cockpit commands and observes; it does not replace operational applications.
Ordinary users work with conventional records, forms, approvals, ledgers, reports, and work queues.
Business objects are authoritative; Agent tasks only advance or analyse them.
All applications share one Kernel, Scheduler, Worker, Runtime, Memory, Approval, and Audit foundation.
Runtime-off applications remain usable; runtime-on applications gain continuous intelligent operation.
Business outcomes must be source-backed and must not be substituted by Agent completion counts.

milestones.title: Application endpoint, persona, navigation and permission registry
Business object to Agent Task and Runner contract
Minimum conventional workbench for six business applications
First validated workflow with business-object write-back
Strategy, HR and Finance domain fields and lifecycle state machines
Strategy, HR and Finance business-object workflows on the shared Kernel
Growth & Sales, Manufacturing ERP and Smart Park domain records and workflows
Move authoritative business records and work items to isolated transactional PostgreSQL
Domain record detail pages, approval inbox and source-backed application reports

next_recommended_action.title: Implement business detail, approval and reporting surfaces
next_recommended_action.reason: Authoritative records, work items and audit events now use scoped transactional PostgreSQL with CAS, idempotency, restart recovery and atomic Runtime write-back. Normal users next need record detail pages, approval inboxes and source-backed domain reports.

stop_policy: Stop on business-object boundary violations, duplicate runtime stacks, permission bypass, unvalidated write-back, secret exposure, or failed release checks.
